newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister rules out referendum on euro.
newsitem.headline: French minister rules out referendum on euro.

text.p: France's new leftist government does not intend to hold a referendum on whether Paris should proceed to European economic and monetary union, Parliamentary Relations Minister Daniel Vaillant said on Sunday.
Vaillant, in an interview on France 2 television, said he was clarifying a widely misinterpreted remark made by Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin in an interview on the same station on Thursday.
"He was not talking about a referendum in his remarks on France 2," Vaillant said.

Jospin, whose leftist government took power five weeks ago from the previous rightist government, had said he would "sound out" the French people if he had to choose between the terms for a single European currency and preserving economic growth.
Jospin aides had earlier said on Friday that the statement did not refer to a referendum.
"He was not talking about a formal consultation of the French people," Vaillant reiterated.
He said the prime minister was instead talking about such tactics as opinion polls and discussions with elected officials and various public groups.
The French Communist Party, a part of the government leftist coalition, backs a referendum before any move to a single European currency.

In this year's parliamentary election campaign Jospin opposed a referendum on the euro, saying the French people had already approved the Maastricht treaty by referendum in September 1992 and France had given its word.
However, Jospin has raised doubts about his new government's commitment to the euro by ruling out further austerity to meet the criteria set out in the Maastricht Treaty for a single currency.
